name: Atari ST
description: Atari Corporation's 16-bit home computer, launched in 1985 shortly after Jack Tramiel took over Atari. It paired a Motorola 68000 with a GEM desktop at a low price. Built-in MIDI ports made it a long-running fixture in music studios.
curiosities: It was nicknamed the "Jackintosh" after Jack Tramiel and its Mac-like desktop.
Built-in MIDI ports made it a common studio computer, and Steinberg's Cubase first appeared on it.
Its desktop was GEM, licensed from Digital Research.
The 1989 STE update added a blitter, a 4,096-colour palette and stereo DMA sound.
Its processor is a Motorola 68000 at 8 MHz.
Its palette has 512 colours, 16 at once in its lowest resolution.
Its sharp black-and-white monitor at 640 × 400 suited desktop publishing and music.
Its sound chip is a Yamaha YM2149.
Dungeon Master first came out on it, in 1987.
TOS, its operating system, stands for The Operating System.
The Falcon030 of 1992 was its successor.
story: After leaving Commodore, Jack Tramiel bought Atari's computer business in 1984 and built a 68000 machine fast and cheaply: the 520ST launched in 1985, with a GUI, a mouse and a price far below a Mac's.

Its built-in MIDI ports made it the standard computer in recording studios, where Cubase was born on it. In Europe it was a games machine too, rivalling the Amiga, with games such as Dungeon Master, Starglider and Carrier Command.
The ST line ran until the Falcon of 1992. Some musicians still use theirs for its tight MIDI timing.
